scope: All 280 main-set nonbasic cards, each read against both written reviews and canonical card rules; 15 lands retain explicit shared-cycle source scope.
format: Limited opinions interpreted for Sealed preparation; not measured Sealed results.

cards.name: Arcane Amphisbaena
cards.why: A deathtouch blocker can protect your life total and a Jace token while adding two loyalty.
cards.better: Better when your deck needs time to develop an empower engine.
cards.watch: It discourages ground attacks but is not a quick way to win.
cards.disagreement: Quinn calls it a strong early play; Josh sees a useful but less exciting two-drop.

cards.name: Fatehold Chronologist // Peer Review
cards.why: A cheap flyer followed by Peer Review develops your board without spending another card.
cards.better: Best when you can spend the next turn on the prepared spell.
cards.watch: Both bodies are small, and the uncast prepared copy is lost if the creature leaves.

cards.name: Bestial Incursion
cards.why: One card can produce two trampling 4/4s over separate turns.
cards.better: Self-mill or discard can give you access to the flashback without casting it from hand.
cards.watch: The second cast costs six mana; you still need early plays.

cards.name: Budding Insurgent
cards.why: Vigilance gives you a normal curve play with an artifact or enchantment answer attached.
cards.better: More useful when the opponent has an important target; a legendary enchantment also replaces the sacrificed card.
cards.watch: The sacrifice ability is sorcery-speed, and using it gives up your creature.
cards.disagreement: Quinn starts lower because he questions target availability; Josh values the acceptable body and incidental upside.

cards.name: Generous Revival
cards.why: Returns a small creature with an extra counter and can be cast again through flashback.
cards.better: Look for useful creatures with mana value three or less, especially worthwhile enters abilities.
cards.watch: It needs a target already in the graveyard, and the five-mana flashback is slow.
cards.disagreement: Quinn is sceptical of the setup and mana cost; Josh sees a playable two-for-one in the right deck.

cards.name: Twinned Vision
cards.why: Provides two spell casts from one card, useful when casting spells generates additional value.
cards.better: Improves with spell payoffs or ways to discard or mill it.
cards.watch: The hand cast only draws one card; flashback also requires discarding a card.
cards.disagreement: Quinn wants discard or self-mill support; Josh is more receptive to its card flow in spell-heavy decks.

cards.name: Void Extrapolator // Omit Variables
cards.why: An early creature that supplies a prepared mill spell and grows at threshold.
cards.better: Prioritise it when reaching seven graveyard cards benefits several cards in your deck.
cards.watch: Outside a graveyard plan, the body and self-mill are much less compelling.
cards.disagreement: Quinn highlights its importance to the self-mill deck; Josh puts more emphasis on how much support it needs.

cards.name: Whiplash Wordsmith // Vicious Verse
cards.why: Its prepared ping can enable flying and haste for an immediate attack.
cards.better: Other sources of noncombat damage can enable later attacks without relying on the one-shot prepared spell.
cards.watch: Casting the creature and its prepared spell in one turn costs five mana. Both reviewers question that rate.

cards.name: Memory Trap
cards.why: Three mana answers an opposing nonland permanent, including a planeswalker.
cards.better: Useful when your other answers cannot handle a particular permanent type.
cards.watch: The exiled permanent returns if the enchantment leaves the battlefield.

cards.name: Extended Absence
cards.why: Instant-speed exile answers a creature or planeswalker; the damage and life gain can also trigger payoffs.
cards.better: Especially useful alongside noncombat-damage or life-gain rewards.
cards.watch: Four-mana answers can crowd your curve. Leave room for cheaper interaction.
cards.disagreement: Both value it highly; Josh specifically cautions against loading up on too many four-mana removal spells.

cards.name: Last Gasp
cards.why: Efficiently removes small creatures or shrinks a larger creature during combat.
cards.better: A blocker or another source of damage can help finish a creature it cannot kill alone.
cards.watch: It gives −3/−3, so an undamaged 4/4 becomes a 1/1 and survives.

cards.name: Wrath of the Bloodmane
cards.why: Four damage can answer a creature or a Jace token even without the discount.
cards.better: A legendary creature reduces the cost by one generic mana.
cards.watch: An empower Jace token is a planeswalker, not a legendary creature, and does not enable the discount.
cards.disagreement: Quinn likes the undiscounted rate; Josh finds it less exciting than removal that also generates extra value.

cards.name: Yoshimaru, Scrappy Stray
cards.why: Adds a body while another creature you control fights an opposing creature.
cards.better: Best with a large creature or deathtoucher already on your battlefield.
cards.watch: Yoshimaru cannot be its own fighter. Opposing interaction can spoil the fight.
cards.disagreement: Quinn is particularly enthusiastic about recurring the enters ability; Josh stresses that fighting is riskier than one-sided damage.

cards.name: Vigorbloom Charm
cards.why: Can protect a permanent, draw a card and gain life, or grow a creature before it fights.
cards.better: Holding it up is useful when either protection or a fight would change the next exchange.
cards.watch: You need both colours, and the fight mode still needs a suitable creature.

cards.name: Prudent Fateseer // Peer Review
cards.why: Peer Review supplies a second body, while scry or surveil can boost your team before combat.
cards.better: Gets better with several attackers and reliable ways to scry or surveil.
cards.watch: The +1/+0 boost happens only once each turn and does little on an empty board.
cards.disagreement: Quinn gives little credit to the small boost; Josh sees more upside when the deck can go wide and trigger it reliably.

cards.name: Woodwork Prodigy // Soul Tether
cards.why: Can prepare again each upkeep and keep producing Heartwood tokens over multiple turns.
cards.better: Needs expensive spells, artifact uses or mana sinks worth accelerating into.
cards.watch: Each Soul Tether still costs three mana, and the creature supplies no payoff for the accumulated mana.
cards.disagreement: Quinn is very enthusiastic about repeated Heartwoods; Josh ties its value more closely to the deck’s ramp targets and mana sinks.

cards.name: Way of the Mind Sculptor
cards.why: Adds loyalty and rewards loyalty activations that remove at least two counters.
cards.better: Additional empower sources or planeswalkers help turn the initial investment into repeated draws.
cards.watch: Five mana does not add a blocker. A weak board or too little support can leave this slow enchantment stranded.
cards.disagreement: Quinn doubts the investment will pay off; Josh sees a higher ceiling with additional empower support.

cards.name: Murmuring Volume
cards.why: Supplies any colour and can exchange an unwanted card for a new draw later.
cards.better: Consider it for a slower deck that needs fixing, ramp or artifact support.
cards.watch: Spending turn three on a mana rock can leave you behind. Most straightforward two-colour decks may not need it.

cards.name: Room of Refuge
cards.why: Chooses the colour your mana base needs and offers a late use when another land is less valuable.
cards.better: Useful for a missing colour source without needing a basic of that colour in your deck.
cards.watch: It enters tapped, only makes the chosen colour, and its counter ability costs five mana plus the land itself.
cards.disagreement: Quinn usually prefers a dual land; Josh considers the fixing and late utility a closer comparison.

cards.name: Hungering Puppetbeast
cards.why: Brings the artifact it needs to grow and gain haste, trample or hexproof.
cards.better: Keeping one mana and another artifact available preserves the option to respond to removal.
cards.watch: Each activation consumes another artifact. Spending the Heartwood to attack immediately uses up that protection resource.

cards.name: Garruk, Veiled Butcher
cards.why: Can weaken an attacker, trade a small creature for a Beast, or attack the opponent’s hand.
cards.better: Small expendable creatures improve the sacrifice mode; a protected board lets him generate value over several turns.
cards.watch: The sacrifice mode affects you too, and −4/−1 does not kill most large creatures.

cards.name: Chandra, Torch of Defiance
cards.why: Can immediately deal four damage to a creature, then generate cards, damage or mana on later turns.
cards.better: A stable board and a reliable red base help you protect and cast her.
cards.watch: She cannot both use removal and her card-advantage ability in the same turn. Her removal targets creatures, not planeswalkers.
cards.disagreement: Both reviewers are enthusiastic. Josh reserves his highest grade for planeswalkers that generate value and protect themselves at the same time.

cards.name: Greenhouse Propagator
cards.why: Produces mana and turns later creatures entering into life-gain triggers.
cards.better: Life-gain payoffs make those triggers valuable beyond the extra life.
cards.watch: A three-mana ramp creature can be inefficient when the deck has no life-gain rewards.
cards.disagreement: Quinn expects several decks to want it; Josh wants multiple life-gain payoffs before valuing it highly.

cards.name: Emrakul, the Exigent Doom
cards.why: Flying, trample and a cast trigger that untaps your lands offer a spectacular late play.
cards.better: Requires a realistic route to ten mana and a deck that survives long enough to use it.
cards.watch: Both reviewers are sceptical: the mana investment is enormous, and an opponent may pay ward by sacrificing spare lands.

cards.name: Academic Ascent
cards.why: Pump and flying can win combat while adding loyalty.
cards.better: Other empower sources turn the two loyalty into a draw.
cards.watch: Two loyalty alone cannot pay for a card draw.
cards.disagreement: Quinn values the extra resource; Josh finds both the trick and empower amount underwhelming.

cards.name: Blossom-Blessed Angel // Seed Suture
cards.why: Flying and vigilance let it attack while holding off attackers.
cards.better: Seed Suture improves the body or enables life-gain payoffs.
cards.watch: The prepared spell needs another mana and the creature to remain in play.

cards.name: Campus Crier
cards.why: Three power pressures opponents and Jace tokens.
cards.better: Death, discard or milling leaves a later empower activation.
cards.watch: One toughness makes opposing small creatures effective blockers.

cards.name: Enlightened Confidant
cards.why: Lifelink can enable end-step selection and extra cards.
cards.better: Repeated life gain raises the mana value of cards you can recover.
cards.watch: Without life gain, it is only a small lifelinker.

cards.name: Fateshaper Aspirant
cards.why: Can recover a legendary card or help an existing creature attack.
cards.better: A strong legend in your graveyard makes the expensive body worthwhile.
cards.watch: Five-drops compete for scarce space in your curve.

cards.name: Flickering Hound
cards.why: Creature spells can repeatedly flicker another creature for value.
cards.better: Useful enters abilities make each subsequent creature more rewarding.
cards.watch: The four-mana body is small and vulnerable without good targets.

cards.name: Germinate Recruits
cards.why: A large life-gain turn can produce several Cadets.
cards.better: Large lifelink hits leave mana available for the follow-up spell.
cards.watch: Small life-gain triggers produce little; no life gained means no tokens.

cards.name: Graft Surgeon
cards.why: Can pass its counters to another creature when it dies.
cards.better: Additional counters increase what survives the trade.
cards.watch: You need another creature to receive them; exile avoids the death trigger.
cards.disagreement: Quinn likes the transferable counters; Josh sees ordinary filler.

cards.name: Guiding Hydra
cards.why: Converts its own counters into permanent growth for other creatures.
cards.better: A wide board makes each combat trigger much stronger.
cards.watch: Removal before combat can leave no value, and each trigger shrinks the Hydra.

cards.name: Hexhaven Battalion
cards.why: Three bodies and empower help rebuild a depleted board.
cards.better: Basic landcycling makes it useful when you need a land instead.
cards.watch: The full spell costs six mana including double white.

cards.name: Kindred Judgment
cards.why: Can remove much of the opposing board while sparing a chosen type.
cards.better: Your creatures sharing a type can make the wipe more favourable.
cards.watch: Seven mana is slow, and opponents may share the type you spare.

cards.name: Loyal Tutor
cards.why: Finds a specific planeswalker for your next draw.
cards.better: Only exceptional planeswalkers justify considering the card disadvantage.
cards.watch: It puts the card on top, not into your hand, and needs a real target.
cards.disagreement: Quinn rejects the card cost; Josh would consider it for an exceptional planeswalker.

cards.name: Predictive Preparations
cards.why: Can grow two creatures now and again through flashback.
cards.better: Wide attacking boards and counter payoffs make the counters matter.
cards.watch: It needs creatures already in play, and the second cast costs four mana.
cards.disagreement: Quinn expects useful support; Josh is much more sceptical of the rate.

cards.name: Prophesied End
cards.why: Kills an attacking creature without giving its controller a card.
cards.better: Defensive decks can wait for a target to attack.
cards.watch: Killing a nonattacker lets its controller draw.
cards.disagreement: Quinn values the flexibility; Josh prefers it mainly in controlling decks.

cards.name: Refute Destiny
cards.why: Cheaply exiles green or blue creatures and planeswalkers.
cards.better: Blue Jace tokens provide targets even outside blue decks.
cards.watch: Check the target's colour; this cannot answer other threats.
cards.disagreement: Quinn sees broader utility through Jace tokens; Josh prefers the sideboard.

cards.name: Repurposed Enforcer
cards.why: Attacking can generate loyalty even if the creature later trades.
cards.better: More creatures increase the loyalty gained per attack.
cards.watch: It contributes little while defending or when your board is empty.

cards.name: Return to the Light Realms
cards.why: Returns all your nonland permanents from the graveyard.
cards.better: Only very slow games with a stocked graveyard favour it.
cards.watch: Nine mana is a huge commitment without a guaranteed win.
cards.disagreement: Quinn would avoid it; Josh allows a narrow slow-matchup sideboard role.

cards.name: Shatterwing Pegasus
cards.why: Can attack in the air and later pump your whole team.
cards.better: A wide board makes the five-mana activation meaningful.
cards.watch: The small flyer and expensive activation are inefficient in isolation.
cards.disagreement: Quinn sees potential in wide decks; Josh is considerably less enthusiastic.

cards.name: Surgical Precision
cards.why: Destroys a large-toughness creature with a life-gain bonus.
cards.better: Life-gain payoffs reward either mode.
cards.watch: Cannot remove small creatures, but its draw mode avoids being stranded.

cards.name: Unflinching Hortimancer
cards.why: Repeated life gain adds permanent counters.
cards.better: Several reliable life-gain sources let it grow through normal play.
cards.watch: Without those sources it is a weak creature, and ward only taxes by one.

cards.name: Your Fate Ends Here
cards.why: Answers creatures or planeswalkers costing at least three and surveils.
cards.better: Useful when your cheap removal cannot handle expensive threats.
cards.watch: Cannot target two-drops or ordinary zero-mana-value Jace tokens.

cards.name: Countersculpt
cards.why: Counters any spell while adding a loyalty counter.
cards.better: Controlling or revealing a Jace avoids the extra generic mana.
cards.watch: Budget the additional mana when you cannot behold a Jace.

cards.name: Cruel Calculations
cards.why: Can draw several cards after a substantial mill effect.
cards.better: Omit Variables supplies three milled cards to count that turn.
cards.watch: Needs same-turn setup and mana; it can otherwise draw nothing.
cards.disagreement: Quinn likes the self-mill ceiling; Josh considers the setup too unreliable.

cards.name: Cryotheory Adept
cards.why: Offers an early body and a later tap-and-stun effect.
cards.better: Self-mill can make the graveyard ability available without casting it.
cards.watch: The body is fragile and the graveyard activation costs four mana.

cards.name: Diviner of Victory // Unwind History
cards.why: Selection triggers grow it temporarily; its prepared spell can clear a small blocker.
cards.better: Frequent scry or surveil can enable larger attacks.
cards.watch: The bounce only hits opposing creatures with mana value three or less.
cards.disagreement: Quinn likes the aggressive upside; Josh finds the restrictions limiting.

cards.name: Divining Duelist
cards.why: Can tap a blocker, untap a defender or filter a card.
cards.better: Fits turns where you hold up interaction and need a fallback play.
cards.watch: The body is modest; tapping does not permanently answer a threat.

cards.name: Icy Reception
cards.why: Counters a creature or legendary spell unless its controller pays three.
cards.better: The power-reduction mode can rescue combat after a creature resolves.
cards.watch: Opponents can pay the tax later; neither mode is unconditional removal.

cards.name: Infinite Coursework
cards.why: Taps a creature, removes its abilities and takes away its prepared spell.
cards.better: Particularly useful against creatures with valuable ongoing abilities.
cards.watch: The creature remains on the battlefield; removing the Aura can release it.

cards.name: Jace's Machinations
cards.why: Can enable a draw on the opponent's turn and another on yours.
cards.better: Granted loyalty abilities give the eight counters additional uses.
cards.watch: Still respect one loyalty activation per planeswalker per turn.

cards.name: Mindseeker Oculus
cards.why: Four loyalty can immediately fund a draw and leave one counter.
cards.better: Additional empower or loyalty payoffs extend that value.
cards.watch: Drawing spends loyalty; keeping the Jace alive requires protection.

cards.name: Perfected Theory
cards.why: Can shrink a threat or enlarge your creature for one mana.
cards.better: Combat lets a size change turn into an actual trade.
cards.watch: It sets base stats, not counters or other bonuses, and invites interaction.

cards.name: Plan for All Outcomes
cards.why: Moves a nonland permanent to its owner's library and rewards later noncreature spells.
cards.better: Casting noncreature spells on both turns produces more loyalty.
cards.watch: The opponent chooses top or bottom; it is not permanent removal.

cards.name: Precise Redaction
cards.why: Efficiently counters white or black spells.
cards.better: Bring it in when the opponent has worthwhile targets.
cards.watch: It is dead against spells of other colours.
cards.disagreement: Quinn considers main-deck use with discard outlets; Josh strongly prefers the sideboard.

cards.name: Protege's Awakening
cards.why: Draws immediately and adds enough loyalty for two normal Jace draws.
cards.better: A defended Jace or granted loyalty ability improves the investment.
cards.watch: You cannot spend both normal draw activations in the same turn.

cards.name: Seasoned Cryomancer
cards.why: Filters two cards and can stun creatures when you discard nonlands.
cards.better: Discardable flashback cards and self-mill improve both halves.
cards.watch: The enters ability draws before discarding, even with an empty hand.

cards.name: Semester Foreseer // Peer Review
cards.why: Surveils on entry and offers a prepared Cadet plus another surveil.
cards.better: Selection payoffs benefit from the separate surveil events.
cards.watch: The complete package requires seven mana over multiple casts.

cards.name: Sphinx of False Conclusions
cards.why: Can trade in combat and leave a replacement flyer.
cards.better: Holding up mana lets you threaten interaction or a flash blocker.
cards.watch: Exile and ability-removing Auras can bypass the death-trigger value.

cards.name: Sphinx's Approach
cards.why: Trades one card for two at instant speed.
cards.better: Slower blue decks can leave up interaction before drawing.
cards.watch: Double blue is restrictive; do not plan around assembling five copies.

cards.name: Surveillance Phantasm
cards.why: Flying and vigilance let it attack and still defend after selection.
cards.better: Cheap scry or surveil avoids paying four mana to enable attacks.
cards.watch: Without selection it has defender.
cards.disagreement: Quinn questions the small payoff; Josh values flying, vigilance and the mana sink more.

cards.name: The Theorist, Jace Beleren
cards.why: Draws on opponents' draw steps while its loyalty abilities affect the board.
cards.better: Blockers and interaction help sustain the repeated draws.
cards.watch: Bounce is temporary, and opposing attacks or removal can still end the engine.

cards.name: Theorist's Proxy
cards.why: A small blocker arrives with enough loyalty for a Jace draw.
cards.better: Holding up mana preserves options; spare loyalty can support larger abilities.
cards.watch: The sacrifice ability matters only against counterspells.

cards.name: Undulating Witness
cards.why: Basic landcycling fixes early mana; later it can be a flyer.
cards.better: Useful when a deck needs fixing but cannot afford a dead late draw.
cards.watch: The creature is expensive and pumping it reduces toughness.

cards.name: Unsummon
cards.why: Can save your creature, remove a token or disrupt combat.
cards.better: An aggressive attack or valuable enters ability increases its impact.
cards.watch: Returning a nontoken enemy is temporary and usually costs a card.

cards.name: Variable Chaser // Arc of Fortune
cards.why: A flying prowess creature can turn noncreature spells into damage.
cards.better: A nearly empty hand makes its prepared refill more attractive.
cards.watch: The opponent can also choose to draw seven; evaluate their hand first.
cards.disagreement: Quinn likes the body more; Josh views it largely as modest flying filler.

cards.name: Apex Witchstalker
cards.why: Basic landcycling finds a needed land before the expensive creature is cast.
cards.better: Life-gain payoffs and reanimation give the other abilities extra value.
cards.watch: Six mana and double black make the creature a slow fallback.

cards.name: Bloodline Recollector // Ancestral Craving
cards.why: Three creature deaths can unlock a very cheap three-card draw.
cards.better: Combat trades and sacrifice effects can supply the required deaths.
cards.watch: It enters unprepared; fewer than three deaths leave only the body.

cards.name: Break Under Pressure
cards.why: Makes the opponent sacrifice a creature or planeswalker with greatest mana value.
cards.better: Answers protected expensive threats without targeting them.
cards.watch: Greatest mana value is not always their best permanent; ties let them choose.

cards.name: Cast Away Doubt
cards.why: Draws two cards while damaging both players.
cards.better: Noncombat-damage payoffs give the opponent's damage extra value.
cards.watch: It costs life and does not develop your board.

cards.name: Dark Matter Manipulator
cards.why: Mills three on entry and gains power as the graveyard grows.
cards.better: Several graveyard payoffs make the milling useful beyond its own size.
cards.watch: Without graveyard value the small body is unimpressive.
cards.disagreement: Quinn is enthusiastic about the enabler; Josh wants meaningful payoffs, not just more mill.

cards.name: Darklight Phoenix
cards.why: Flying and haste pressure opponents; two precombat deaths can return it.
cards.better: Sacrifice-plus-removal effects make the death condition easier.
cards.watch: Deaths during combat are too late for that turn's beginning-of-combat trigger.

cards.name: Extrapolate the Impossible
cards.why: Can obtain one of two differently named cards from your event sideboard.
cards.better: Only worthwhile if both offered cards solve the current problem.
cards.watch: The opponent chooses, and most of your strongest cards already belong in your deck.

cards.name: Lich's Relic
cards.why: Paying the enters cost destroys a creature or planeswalker and leaves a reusable boost.
cards.better: Later creatures can carry the Equipment after the removal is spent.
cards.watch: Budget three total mana for the removal; equipping costs another two.

cards.name: Multiply by Zero
cards.why: Setting base toughness to zero kills many creatures cheaply.
cards.better: Even surviving creatures may become easier to defeat in combat.
cards.watch: Counters and other toughness bonuses can keep the creature alive.

cards.name: Overwrite the Multiverse
cards.why: Exiles all creatures and leaves loyalty based on the number exiled.
cards.better: A defensive deck can recover from a crowded opposing board.
cards.watch: It costs six, exiles your creatures too and leaves planeswalkers untouched.

cards.name: Rampart Hunter
cards.why: An enters boost and deathtouch can make another creature hard to block profitably.
cards.better: An existing attacker, particularly a trampler, uses the temporary bonus.
cards.watch: The four-mana body is modest when there is no useful attack.

cards.name: Rank Rat
cards.why: Makes the opponent discard while providing a small creature.
cards.better: Sacrifice or recursion can use the body after its initial value.
cards.watch: An empty opposing hand removes the discard benefit; the body attacks poorly.

cards.name: Rewrite Regrets
cards.why: Returns an eligible creature or planeswalker and adds loyalty.
cards.better: Landcyclers and self-mill provide natural graveyard targets.
cards.watch: Needs a worthwhile target already in the graveyard, with mana value at most six.
cards.disagreement: Josh likes the rate broadly; Quinn is more cautious about target availability.

cards.name: Rise of the Deathbringer
cards.why: Can shrink the whole board or turn a large creature's power into cards.
cards.better: Combat damage can help the −3/−3 mode finish larger threats.
cards.watch: Your creatures also shrink, and the draw mode can cost substantial life.

cards.name: Sanctum Lurker
cards.why: Gives planeswalkers a loyalty-building drain ability and lets them survive zero loyalty.
cards.better: Empower sources and drain payoffs increase its continuing value.
cards.watch: Losing this creature removes those granted abilities and zero-loyalty protection.

cards.name: Screeching Soulbreaker
cards.why: Attacking triggers damage and life gain without requiring a successful hit.
cards.better: Life-gain or noncombat-damage payoffs multiply the attack's value.
cards.watch: The small body is less appealing without those synergies.

cards.name: Silence the Echo
cards.why: Destroys a creature or planeswalker for two mana plus a sacrifice, or five mana.
cards.better: Expendable creatures or low-loyalty Jace tokens reduce the effective cost.
cards.watch: The sacrifice is a real resource cost; the five-mana mode is slow.
cards.disagreement: Quinn likes sacrificing spare Jace tokens; Josh questions the rate and setup.

cards.name: Solve for Disappointment
cards.why: Takes a nonland permanent from the opponent's hand and adds loyalty.
cards.better: Early casting can remove a threat before it reaches the battlefield.
cards.watch: Cannot take instants or sorceries, and late empty hands give no discard value.

cards.name: Terminal Criticism
cards.why: Cheaply destroys blue or red creatures and planeswalkers.
cards.better: Jace tokens provide blue targets even outside blue decks.
cards.watch: It cannot answer permanents of other colours.
cards.disagreement: Quinn considers main-deck use because of Jace; Josh treats it as a sideboard card.

cards.name: Theoretical Necromancer
cards.why: Can later return another creature from your graveyard to hand.
cards.better: Self-mill or discard accesses that value without casting the fragile creature.
cards.watch: The four-mana activation returns to hand, not the battlefield.

cards.name: Vraska's Final Mercy
cards.why: Cheaply destroys a creature or planeswalker, with empower as an alternative.
cards.better: A black base makes the double-black cost reliable.
cards.watch: Both modes cost two life, and the spell is sorcery-speed.

cards.name: Ajani's Anguish
cards.why: Can remove a blocker or finish an opponent, then gives your team trample.
cards.better: Ramp and large attacking creatures improve both halves.
cards.watch: Damage scales inefficiently against large creatures.
cards.disagreement: Quinn finds it inefficient outside ramp; Josh values the finishing flexibility and lasting trample.

cards.name: Artifist Acumen
cards.why: Replaces itself while giving your team first strike.
cards.better: Prowess creatures and multi-creature combats give it extra impact.
cards.watch: It provides no power boost without other effects.

cards.name: Awaken the Inferno
cards.why: Six damage handles many threats; landcycling finds an early land instead.
cards.better: The counter can develop your board while removing a threat.
cards.watch: Casting it costs five; cycling uses up the removal spell.

cards.name: Blazing Crescendo
cards.role: Pump with a temporary extra card
cards.why: Can increase damage while giving access to another card.
cards.better: Mana available this turn or next helps use the exiled card.
cards.watch: Only one extra toughness may not save your creature; the card access expires.

cards.name: Chandra's Emberling
cards.why: Each noncreature spell adds a permanent counter.
cards.better: Cheap spells let it grow while you develop or interact.
cards.watch: Its initial body is weak without enough noncreature spells.
cards.disagreement: Quinn doubts the baseline; Josh sees considerable upside in a supported deck.

cards.name: Command the Stage
cards.why: Repeated casts make Cadets and grow existing Wizard tokens.
cards.better: Reliable noncombat damage returns the spell to your hand.
cards.watch: The newly created token does not receive its own counter.

cards.name: Craterclaw Colossus
cards.why: Can turn an artifact-heavy board into a large trampling attack.
cards.better: Heartwoods both supply mana and increase the team power boost.
cards.watch: Seven mana including triple red is demanding without ramp and artifacts.

cards.name: Curse-Marred Demon
cards.why: A large flying trampler is useful before counting the search ability.
cards.better: A fuller hand reduces the chance of discarding the card you search for.
cards.watch: The discard is random; an empty hand guarantees discarding the searched card.

cards.name: Draconic Visitor
cards.why: A large flyer also converts new artifact tokens into Dragons.
cards.better: Heartwood creation can become repeated flying threats.
cards.watch: The replacement means you do not receive the original artifact token or its mana ability.

cards.name: Eardrum Rattler
cards.why: Can send another small creature past blockers.
cards.better: Combat-damage triggers or pressure on Jace tokens reward the evasion.
cards.watch: The ability needs a creature with power two or less and taps this creature.
cards.disagreement: Quinn sees useful pressure; Josh mostly sees replaceable curve filler.

cards.name: Essence Burn
cards.why: Five damage with an exile replacement efficiently handles matching targets.
cards.better: Bring it in against black or green creatures and planeswalkers.
cards.watch: It has no targets of other colours.

cards.name: Face Yourself
cards.why: Copies one player's creatures with haste for a potentially powerful turn.
cards.better: Useful creatures and a planeswalker can make the copies persist.
cards.watch: Seven mana is steep; without a planeswalker the copies must be sacrificed at the end step.
cards.disagreement: Quinn rejects the inconsistency; Josh acknowledges a much higher potential payoff.

cards.name: Fulminous Forte
cards.why: Five damage answers a threat, or one damage can clean up an opposing board.
cards.better: Combat can leave several creatures vulnerable to the sweeping mode.
cards.watch: One damage is small; choose the mode for the actual board.

cards.name: Hallway Heckler // Vicious Verse
cards.why: Can exchange unwanted cards and carries a prepared damage spell.
cards.better: Discardable graveyard cards improve the rummaging ability.
cards.watch: Discard happens before drawing, and a three-mana utility creature is slow.

cards.name: Heartstring Puller
cards.why: Supplies a trampling creature and a Cadet.
cards.better: Team pumps, Wizard-token rewards and sacrifice outlets use both bodies.
cards.watch: The trampler has low toughness and trades easily.

cards.name: Identity Echo
cards.why: Can exchange your creature or planeswalker for a random one from the library.
cards.better: Only tightly controlled creature selections make the result predictable.
cards.watch: It costs four per activation and exiles a permanent without guaranteeing an upgrade.

cards.name: Master of Barbs
cards.why: Menace pressures opponents while noncombat damage pumps your whole team.
cards.better: Repeatable damage triggers and a wide board multiply its impact.
cards.watch: The power bonus is temporary and requires noncombat damage first.

cards.name: No Admittance
cards.why: Three damage to any target also leaves a loyalty counter.
cards.better: The damage can trigger payoffs or finish a player or Jace token.
cards.watch: Sorcery timing prevents using it as surprise combat interaction.

cards.name: Pompous Battlemage // Improvised Act
cards.why: Provides an early body and a prepared rummage spell.
cards.better: Cheap noncreature spells make the small body more threatening.
cards.watch: Its base body is small and the rummage does not gain a card.
cards.disagreement: Quinn is sceptical of the small body; Josh finds more use in the flexibility.

cards.name: Pyre Rhymer // Molten Tide
cards.why: A substantial prowess body carries a cheap prepared spell.
cards.better: Mountains can turn the prepared mana effect into a larger follow-up turn.
cards.watch: Count untapped Mountains and actual mana needs; the effect does not draw a card.

cards.name: Skilled Battlecarver
cards.why: First strike on your turn and pump make blocking awkward.
cards.better: Mana left available lets you threaten pump without spending it.
cards.watch: It loses first strike on the opponent's turn.

cards.name: Stingcaster Mage
cards.why: Can reuse a graveyard instant or sorcery while adding a hasty body.
cards.better: Cheap removal and other useful spells make good targets.
cards.watch: You still pay the spell's cost and must cast it that turn.

cards.name: Tether Technician
cards.why: Can turn a spare card into two damage on entry.
cards.better: Extra lands or graveyard cards reduce the discard's cost.
cards.watch: Five mana is expensive, and the damage needs a discard.
cards.disagreement: Quinn likes its immediate impact; Josh considers it replaceable top-end filler.

cards.name: Violent Echoes
cards.why: Six damage can answer a threat and turn excess into loyalty.
cards.better: Small targets or already damaged creatures may yield more loyalty.
cards.watch: Do not target a lesser threat just to chase the bonus.

cards.name: Carnivorous Cultivator // Enroot
cards.why: A cheap deathtoucher can recover a land after hitting a player.
cards.better: The prepared spell can put a desired land into the graveyard.
cards.watch: The search puts the land in the graveyard, not your hand; combat damage is needed to recover it.

cards.name: Compel Brutality
cards.why: A creature's power or a planeswalker's loyalty becomes damage, so your board determines what this can kill.
cards.better: Keep a large creature or a well-stocked planeswalker available; deathtouch makes the creature mode particularly effective.
cards.watch: Removing your chosen source in response can spoil the removal.

cards.name: Flourishing Grapple
cards.role: Sideboard removal for red and white
cards.why: One mana can remove a red or white threat while stripping its protective abilities for the turn.
cards.better: Bring it in against eligible targets when your creatures have enough power to kill them.
cards.watch: It needs both your own creature and an opposing red or white creature or planeswalker.

cards.name: Gardenize
cards.why: You spend mana before gaining anything, then need creatures to die before this starts producing mana.
cards.better: Repeated creature deaths and expensive mana sinks give the extra mana somewhere to go.
cards.watch: Both reviewers doubt that the delayed mana repays the card and early turn spent on it.

cards.name: Heartwood Crafter // Soul Tether
cards.why: Its restricted mana can pay for prepared spells, flashback and abilities, and its own prepared spell makes another mana source.
cards.better: A deck with several ways to spend mana outside spells cast from hand uses it best.
cards.watch: Its mana cannot cast spells from your hand; check the restriction before planning a curve.

cards.name: Hexhaven Invigorator
cards.role: A powerful but demanding green threat
cards.why: A large vigilant creature can punish damage-based answers with a huge burst of lands.
cards.better: A heavily green mana base makes four green symbols realistic.
cards.watch: Non-damage removal gets around its land-search trigger.
cards.disagreement: Quinn is deterred by the mana cost and clean removal answers; Josh rates the payoff much more highly when you can cast it.

cards.name: Hunter's Axe
cards.why: Extra power plus your choice of trample or deathtouch makes attacking creatures harder to block profitably.
cards.better: Use it when you can afford the equip cost and keep sending creatures into combat.
cards.watch: The keyword is granted when the creature attacks; it does not provide deathtouch for an ordinary defensive block.

cards.name: Inspired Tethermage
cards.role: A creature that grows with loyalty
cards.why: Adding loyalty counters to your planeswalkers also grows this creature.
cards.better: Cheap, repeated empower effects are better support than relying on its own expensive activation.
cards.watch: Its own empower ability costs six mana, and each triggering event adds only one counter to the creature.

cards.name: Omnipresence
cards.role: An expensive engine with too many conditions
cards.why: Free spells sound attractive, but this costs eight mana and still needs both a wide board and cards in hand.
cards.better: A large creature count and expensive spells remaining in hand are required to exploit it.
cards.watch: Both reviewers would rather spend that mana on a threat that helps immediately.

cards.name: Puppet Crafting
cards.role: Turn a spare permanent into a threat
cards.why: Two mana can turn an artifact or a non-Aura enchantment into a 5/5, giving otherwise modest permanents a new job.
cards.better: Heartwoods and other expendable targets reduce the cost of committing a second card.
cards.watch: Target removal can disrupt the Aura; returning it from the graveyard costs five mana.

cards.name: Restore with Empathy
cards.why: Returning a useful permanent lets you reuse a threat while four life buys time.
cards.better: A strong permanent already in your graveyard makes this a useful late-game draw.
cards.watch: It cannot return instants or sorceries, and trading this card for another is selection rather than extra cards.

cards.name: Simulacrum Shaper
cards.role: Ramp with value on the way out
cards.why: It supplies a tapped basic land on arrival and a card when it dies, helping you reach larger threats.
cards.better: A green base that wants to play longer games uses both halves well.
cards.watch: Exile avoids the death trigger, and the double-green cost matters for early casting.

cards.name: Something Worth Saving
cards.why: Milling four can stock the graveyard while returning a permanent from those cards to your hand.
cards.better: Self-mill payoffs make the cards left behind useful too.
cards.watch: You can miss a permanent. If you take one, normally only three of the milled cards remain in the graveyard.

cards.name: Sureshot Sower
cards.role: Early pressure or an answer to a flyer
cards.why: A cheap reach creature can attack early, while its discard ability gives it a different job later.
cards.better: Keep it in hand when an opposing flyer is the bigger problem than developing another small creature.
cards.watch: The removal ability discards it from your hand; a Sower already on the battlefield cannot use that mode.

cards.name: Tarmogoyf
cards.role: A cheap threat that counts card types
cards.why: Both graveyards contribute to its size, so it can become large for two mana.
cards.better: Self-mill and a variety of card types help it grow earlier.
cards.watch: Many cards of the same type do not make it bigger, and it has no evasion or trample by itself.

cards.name: Tethermage's Advantage
cards.role: A small trick with a surprise block
cards.why: Untapping and granting reach can turn a tapped creature into an unexpected answer to a flyer.
cards.better: A combat where the extra two power and toughness changes the result gives the card a clear purpose.
cards.watch: It depends on a creature and a favourable combat; removal in response can waste it.

cards.name: Verdant Kraken
cards.role: A late threat that keeps making bodies
cards.why: Creating a 3/3 on each player's upkeep can take over a long game.
cards.better: Ramp and a reliable green mana base help you reach seven mana before falling behind.
cards.watch: It makes no token on entry; you must reach an upkeep, and newly created land creatures have summoning sickness.

cards.name: Vinelasher Adept
cards.role: Early fixing with a late creature attached
cards.why: Basic landcycling smooths your mana, while the six-mana creature supplies reach and movable counters.
cards.better: Decide early whether hitting your land drops matters more than saving the late threat.
cards.watch: Six mana is a substantial cost; do not keep a shaky hand just because you want to cast the creature later.

cards.name: Wrecking Gecko
cards.role: A large filler creature and mana sink
cards.why: A 5/5 with ward can fill the top of a curve, with a costly trample boost for stalled games.
cards.better: A deck short of large creatures can use it without additional synergy.
cards.watch: The boost costs eight mana, and ward is a tax rather than immunity to removal.

cards.name: Aerid Konstrari
cards.role: An evasive threat that leaves resources
cards.why: A large flyer brings a Heartwood on arrival and another when it dies, supporting continued development.
cards.better: A red-green base can use the body and the extra mana resources reliably.
cards.watch: Its activated ability is expensive, and exile prevents the death trigger.

cards.name: Avatar of Burgeoning Echoes
cards.why: Each land supplies two loyalty counters, helping planeswalkers keep using their abilities.
cards.better: Planeswalkers already in play and ways to keep making land drops make this an engine.
cards.watch: Empower needs a planeswalker to receive the counters; the granted minus-ten ability is a bonus, not a reliable early plan.

cards.name: Blessed Ghoul
cards.why: Lifelink and a graveyard return ability give a small body repeated uses as fodder or a blocker.
cards.better: Sacrifice, self-mill and lifegain payoffs make each trip through the battlefield count.
cards.watch: Returning it and casting it again both cost mana; a plain 1/1 does little in a deck without those uses.

cards.name: Bloombrute
cards.why: It rewards gaining life with a card and eventually supplies its own lifelink enabler.
cards.better: Cheap lifegain effects let you draw without spending six mana on its ability.
cards.watch: The draw trigger happens only once each turn, even if you gain life several times.

cards.name: Charge the Sanctum
cards.role: A flexible but costly combat trick
cards.why: It can push damage through a wide attack or improve one creature's combat and leave a counter.
cards.better: An established board gives you a choice of useful modes.
cards.watch: Three mana is a lot to leave open, and neither mode helps much without creatures.
cards.disagreement: Quinn is sceptical of the three-mana trick; Josh is more receptive to its flexible single-creature mode.

cards.name: Clash of Elements
cards.role: Flexible tempo against a nonland permanent
cards.why: It moves a permanent off the battlefield and makes its owner choose between a redraw with damage or the bottom of the library.
cards.better: An aggressive board can exploit the lost tempo even when the opponent chooses to draw the card again.
cards.watch: The opponent chooses where it goes, so it is not guaranteed permanent removal.

cards.name: Craftwork Crusher
cards.role: A ramp payoff with immediate value
cards.why: A large trampler arrives with two useful effects, potentially removing a creature and replacing itself.
cards.better: Ramp and reliable red-green mana help you reach its seven-mana cost.
cards.watch: Choose two arrival effects, not all three; your deck still needs ways to survive the early turns.

cards.name: Denzilore Fatehold
cards.role: A flyer that turns selection into team growth
cards.why: Each scry or surveil event adds a counter to every creature you control, on top of a strong flash flyer.
cards.better: Cheap selection and a developed board can turn one trigger into a major advantage.
cards.watch: The mana cost commits you to white-blue, and you still need selection effects after it resolves.

cards.name: Desperate Futurescribe
cards.role: An evasive threat that improves another attacker
cards.why: At combat it boosts another creature, with a lasting counter if you have scried or surveilled that turn.
cards.better: Use your selection effect before the beginning of combat to earn the permanent counter.
cards.watch: It cannot target itself, and selection after its combat trigger is too late for that trigger.

cards.name: Emergency Phytomedic // Seed Suture
cards.role: A small body with a prepared counter
cards.why: The prepared spell adds a counter and a little life, providing several useful triggers across two payments.
cards.better: Counter and lifegain payoffs give the modest body and spell more purpose.
cards.watch: The spell costs extra mana after the creature, so budget for both parts when planning your turn.

cards.name: Entrust the Spark
cards.why: It can exchange a planeswalker for a stronger planeswalker card from your library.
cards.better: A worthwhile target and an expendable planeswalker must both be in your deck for the exchange to work.
cards.watch: A Jace token is not a card you can search for, and drawing your intended target can leave this without its payoff.

cards.name: Fatehold Charm
cards.why: Card draw with empower, temporary disruption or a team combat boost lets it serve several stages of a game.
cards.better: A white-blue deck with planeswalkers and creatures can make good use of every mode.
cards.watch: Returning a spell or creature buys time; it does not permanently answer a threat that can be cast again.

cards.name: Ferocity of the Hunt
cards.why: Deathtouch and returning your creature after death can turn a trade into value.
cards.better: A useful enters ability or first strike gives the Aura a stronger reason to be in your deck.
cards.watch: It needs the right combat and does not save a creature from exile; both reviewers want more than a generic combat trick.

cards.name: Frostbite Pyromental
cards.role: A one-turn attack that must connect
cards.why: The reward is two cards and damage, but only if it deals combat damage to a player.
cards.better: An open attack or enough help to push through blockers makes the short-lived threat useful.
cards.watch: Blockers or removal can deny the draw, and the double-red blue cost makes early casting demanding.

cards.name: Grim Repriser
cards.role: An early threat with a second life
cards.why: A two-mana prowess creature can return from the graveyard after you deal noncombat damage to an opponent.
cards.better: Reliable cheap damage sources let you use the recursion without delaying your turn.
cards.watch: The return requires both colours and a damage event; the finality counter normally limits it to one return.

cards.name: Ingris Stingerquill
cards.role: An evasive threat that turns attacks into damage
cards.why: Every attacking creature deals a point before combat damage, and the activated ability keeps adding hasty attackers.
cards.better: A wide board produces immediate damage even if Ingris stays back.
cards.watch: It is still vulnerable to removal, and the token ability needs four additional mana.

cards.name: Konstrari Charm
cards.role: A combat trick with a sideboard mode
cards.why: Lasting counters and temporary trample are the usual use, with a strong answer to flyers when needed.
cards.better: Against flyers, the removal mode makes its flexibility more valuable.
cards.watch: Spending a card for three colourless mana is usually poor value unless it enables a decisive play.

cards.name: Konstrari Improviser // Soul Tether
cards.role: A two-drop that can ramp next turn
cards.why: The body develops your board before its prepared spell supplies a Heartwood.
cards.better: Larger red or green threats give the extra mana a clear purpose.
cards.watch: Making the Heartwood takes a separate three-mana payment; it does not arrive with the creature.

cards.name: Kwia Vigorbloom
cards.role: A large lifelink flyer that dominates races
cards.why: Flying, vigilance and lifelink let it attack while defending and swinging the life totals.
cards.better: A reliable green-white mana base and enough early plays help you reach six mana.
cards.watch: Ward makes removal harder, not impossible; the Lotus trigger happens at most once each turn.

cards.name: Mind Meanderer
cards.role: An evasive top-end threat with a fight
cards.why: It can remove a creature on arrival and then attack through the air.
cards.better: Choose a fight it survives, and a Jace planeswalker also gives it vigilance.
cards.watch: Fight damage goes both ways; six mana with double blue is a commitment rather than an easy splash.

cards.name: Null Summoner
cards.role: A threat that takes a card from hand
cards.why: Casting it exiles an opposing nonland card, with the possibility of casting that card yourself at threshold.
cards.better: Play it while the opponent still has a meaningful hand; self-mill supports the later payoff.
cards.watch: An empty opposing hand removes much of its value, and reanimating it does not trigger the cast-dependent ability.

cards.name: Paradox Shaper // Omit Variables
cards.role: Repeatable self-mill for a graveyard deck
cards.why: It prepares on your upkeep to supply another mill spell, and can later recycle cards into your library.
cards.better: Several threshold or graveyard payoffs justify spending mana on the engine.
cards.watch: It does not enter prepared, and milling without useful payoffs can leave you behind on board.

cards.name: Primal Witchstalker
cards.role: Graveyard setup with a ramp opportunity
cards.why: Milling four supports your graveyard plan and can return a land tapped to the battlefield.
cards.better: A land already in your graveyard makes the ramp reliable; the returned land need not be among the four milled.
cards.watch: The mill can miss a land if none was already available, so the ramp is not automatic.

cards.name: Proctor of Potential
cards.why: Its own arrival and later creatures each surveil, improving draws and triggering selection payoffs.
cards.better: A creature-heavy white-blue deck with scry or surveil rewards gets value without spending extra mana per trigger.
cards.watch: Returning it requires another selection effect that turn, and finality normally prevents a further return after it dies.

cards.name: Recursive Recruitment
cards.role: Two bodies now and a larger late-game army
cards.why: The first cast provides a reasonable board, while flashback rewards a stocked graveyard with larger tokens.
cards.better: Self-mill and a game plan that can reach eight mana unlock its strongest use.
cards.watch: Count cards actually in the graveyard for the flashback bonus; do not assume a particular token size.

cards.name: Solarium Sentry
cards.role: An efficient body with incidental lifegain
cards.why: Its size is useful for two mana, and opposing cheap spells can repeatedly supply life.
cards.better: Lifegain payoffs and opponents casting many cheap spells make the trigger particularly relevant.
cards.watch: You do not control when the opponent supplies a trigger; it is not a dependable lifegain enabler on demand.

cards.name: Solitary Cell
cards.role: Cheap removal with a mana-value limit
cards.why: It can exile an opposing small nonland permanent, including noncreatures.
cards.better: White-red decks can use it to remove early threats or awkward low-cost engines.
cards.watch: The permanent returns if the Cell leaves, and the legendary-discard ability is a secondary bonus.

cards.name: Stingerquill Charm
cards.why: Three damage to any target gives a strong baseline; the other modes handle combat or develop your board.
cards.better: First strike with deathtouch can punish a large blocker when direct damage is insufficient.
cards.watch: The combat mode still needs a creature and can be disrupted by removal in response.

cards.name: Stingerquill Voxmancer // Vicious Verse
cards.why: Preparing each upkeep lets a cheap creature repeatedly turn on damage payoffs.
cards.better: Several cards rewarding damage to opponents make the small prepared spell worth its mana.
cards.watch: It does not enter prepared, and repeated one-point spells still consume mana each turn.

cards.name: Stinging Vitriol
cards.role: Early disruption with a damage trigger
cards.why: Taking a nonland card can prevent a future problem while two damage enables other effects.
cards.better: Use it before the opponent empties their hand, especially with noncombat-damage payoffs.
cards.watch: It does not affect creatures already on the battlefield; a late draw may only deal two damage.

cards.name: Tam's Resistance
cards.why: Empower four can support a Jace draw while the creature counter remains.
cards.better: Planeswalker and counter synergies make the small effects more useful together.
cards.watch: This is a sorcery, and drawing through Jace requires a legal loyalty activation; it is not an unconditional draw spell.
cards.disagreement: Quinn finds the potential card replacement worthwhile; Josh wants explicit empower support.

cards.name: Tenured Tethermage
cards.role: Ramp that can become a growing threat
cards.why: Trading a land for two Heartwoods increases future mana and supplies artifacts for its growth ability.
cards.better: Other artifacts and graveyard uses for the sacrificed land add value.
cards.watch: The Heartwoods enter tapped, and using artifacts to grow it competes with using them for mana.

cards.name: Theorix Charm
cards.why: It can answer a small creature, tax a noncreature spell or replace itself while milling.
cards.better: A blue-black graveyard deck gets useful fallback value when neither answer mode fits.
cards.watch: The counter mode misses creature spells and can be paid for; minus two toughness misses large threats.
cards.disagreement: Quinn sees overcosted individual effects; Josh places more value on having three useful choices.

cards.name: Theorix Metamage // Omit Variables
cards.role: A graveyard enabler that becomes a flyer
cards.why: Its prepared mill spell moves you toward threshold, where the creature gains power and flying.
cards.better: Other self-mill makes the upgraded body reliable.
cards.watch: Below seven graveyard cards it is a modest ground creature, and removing graveyard cards can switch the bonus off.

cards.name: Twisted Fates
cards.role: Broad removal that improves your board
cards.why: Destroying a nonland permanent while distributing counters can break a stalled game open.
cards.better: Several creatures in play make the second half a substantial advantage.
cards.watch: Five mana and double white make it harder to cast promptly; it is less rewarding on an empty board.

cards.name: Uldaros Theorix
cards.role: A large flyer with graveyard spells attached
cards.why: Casting it can replay several useful effects while adding a major threat.
cards.better: Self-mill and different card types give you a choice of spells within the six-mana-value allowance.
cards.watch: The total allowance is six, the targets are limited by card type, and reanimation does not trigger the ability.

cards.name: Vigorbloom Vanguard // Seed Suture
cards.role: A flexible counter and vigilance enabler
cards.why: The prepared spell improves a creature and gains life, while counter-bearing creatures gain vigilance.
cards.better: A board with several counters or lifegain payoffs gets more than just an upgraded two-drop.
cards.watch: Casting the prepared spell costs extra mana, and creatures without counters do not get vigilance.
cards.disagreement: Quinn sees ordinary curve filler; Josh rates the combined counter, vigilance and lifegain package more highly.

cards.name: Vindictive Triumph
cards.role: Exile removal with possible extra value
cards.why: It cleanly answers a creature or planeswalker and can briefly reuse a small permanent's arrival effect.
cards.better: Targets with useful enters abilities make the temporary return valuable.
cards.watch: The returned permanent enters tapped and is exiled at the next end step; the white-black-black cost is demanding.

cards.name: Warrior's Blades
cards.why: The arrival damage and lifegain provide value before you spend anything on equipping.
cards.better: Counter-bearing creatures reduce the equip cost and make the remaining artifact easier to use.
cards.watch: Casting and equipping can consume a large part of a turn; the initial three damage must be enough for the target.

cards.name: Afterthought Sentry
cards.role: A flexible two-drop with late evasion
cards.why: It can fit any mana base, gain flying for a payment and attack graveyard resources.
cards.better: Use the attack trigger against flashback or other graveyard value, with flying to keep attacking later.
cards.watch: Paying for flying competes with developing your board.
cards.disagreement: Josh expects this to outperform typical colourless filler; Quinn thinks coloured aggressive options will often be better.

cards.name: Archive Arbiter
cards.role: A colourless flyer with an answer attached
cards.why: It can remove an important noncreature permanent or provide a life buffer.
cards.better: Decks short of top-end threats or answers to planeswalkers and enchantments can use its flexibility.
cards.watch: Six mana is expensive, and its removal mode cannot target a creature or land.

cards.name: Codie, Ravenous Codex
cards.role: A payoff for several prepared spells
cards.why: Copying prepared spells can generate value without ever using the five-colour ability.
cards.better: Several worthwhile prepared spells make the three-mana body a useful engine.
cards.watch: Do not distort your mana base for the activated ability; without prepared spells it is a modest defensive body.

cards.name: The Echoverse Fulcrum
cards.role: A colourless reset with a visible warning
cards.why: Any deck can use it to destroy all creatures, spreading the seven-mana total across turns if needed.
cards.better: A slower deck can hold creatures back and plan its recovery after the sweep.
cards.watch: Playing it early warns your opponent, and the activation is sorcery-speed.

cards.name: Eye of Jace
cards.role: Slow selection for a focused synergy deck
cards.why: Repeated surveil can support selection triggers and fill the graveyard.
cards.better: A deck with enough graveyard or surveil payoffs can turn the repeated selection into more than filtering.
cards.watch: It spends a card without replacing itself and must sacrifice itself when its upkeep check reaches threshold.

cards.name: Keeper of the Quiet Hour
cards.why: The arrival trigger can top up an existing Jace while adding a creature.
cards.better: Other empower effects can bridge the gap to a draw activation.
cards.watch: Two loyalty counters alone are not enough to draw with a new Jace, and the creature's two toughness is fragile.

cards.name: Living Library
cards.role: An early blocker with a late answer
cards.why: A defensive body buys time before you sacrifice it to shuffle away a creature or planeswalker.
cards.better: Slower decks protecting Jace can use both jobs.
cards.watch: It contributes little to an aggressive plan, and the removal activation costs six mana.

cards.name: Medic's Kitesail
cards.why: It can help a ground creature attack over a stall and trigger lifegain rewards.
cards.better: Large ground creatures or several lifegain payoffs justify the equipment investment.
cards.watch: Casting and equipping cost four mana in total, with another equip payment whenever you move it.
cards.disagreement: Quinn sees a situational way through stalls; Josh largely wants lifegain synergies to justify the cost.

cards.name: Dedicated Commons
cards.role: Two-colour fixing with a planeswalker bonus
cards.why: Both reviewers value the cycle for reliable access to two colours; a planeswalker can let it enter untapped.
cards.better: Use it when both colours help your mana base, including a supported splash.
cards.watch: Plan early turns assuming it may enter tapped; controlling a planeswalker is a condition, not a guarantee.

cards.name: Deserted Beach
cards.role: Two-colour fixing for the middle game
cards.why: Both reviewers value the cycle because it usually enters untapped after your first two lands.
cards.better: Use it when its colours support your deck or a carefully supported splash.
cards.watch: It enters tapped if you control fewer than two other lands, which can disrupt an early curve.

cards.name: Fatehold Annex
cards.role: Two-colour fixing with a planeswalker bonus
cards.why: Both reviewers value the cycle for reliable access to two colours; a planeswalker can let it enter untapped.
cards.better: Use it when both colours help your mana base, including a supported splash.
cards.watch: Plan early turns assuming it may enter tapped; controlling a planeswalker is a condition, not a guarantee.

cards.name: Formidable Commons
cards.role: Two-colour fixing with a planeswalker bonus
cards.why: Both reviewers value the cycle for reliable access to two colours; a planeswalker can let it enter untapped.
cards.better: Use it when both colours help your mana base, including a supported splash.
cards.watch: Plan early turns assuming it may enter tapped; controlling a planeswalker is a condition, not a guarantee.

cards.name: Hall of Echoes
cards.why: It can copy your best creature when spare mana would otherwise go unused.
cards.better: A well-fixed mana base and worthwhile creatures make the late-game option more attractive.
cards.watch: It only produces colourless mana, needs a creature to copy and costs five mana to activate.
cards.disagreement: Quinn thinks the cost and dependence on another creature outweigh the upside; Josh is more interested when the mana base can afford it.

cards.name: Haunted Ridge
cards.role: Two-colour fixing for the middle game
cards.why: Both reviewers value the cycle because it usually enters untapped after your first two lands.
cards.better: Use it when its colours support your deck or a carefully supported splash.
cards.watch: It enters tapped if you control fewer than two other lands, which can disrupt an early curve.

cards.name: Hexhaven Dueling Arena
cards.role: A land that reuses prepared spells
cards.why: It can prepare a creature again, with a cheaper activation after that creature attacks.
cards.better: Several strong prepared spells and reliable coloured mana are prerequisites.
cards.watch: It produces only colourless mana, and preparing a creature still leaves the spell's casting cost to pay.
cards.disagreement: Quinn would usually avoid the mana-base cost; Josh sees a home in dedicated prepared-spell decks.

cards.why: Both reviewers value the cycle for reliable access to two colours; a planeswalker can let it enter untapped.
cards.better: Use it when both colours help your mana base, including a supported splash.
cards.watch: Plan early turns assuming it may enter tapped; controlling a planeswalker is a condition, not a guarantee.

cards.better: Use it when its colours support your deck or a carefully supported splash.
cards.watch: It enters tapped if you control fewer than two other lands, which can disrupt an early curve.

cards.name: Roiling Canopy
cards.why: Repeated power boosts become possible only once you have a very large number of Forests.
cards.better: A nearly mono-green deck is the realistic setting for its trigger.
cards.watch: It enters tapped and is not itself a Forest; ordinary two-colour decks may never reach the requirement.

cards.name: Theorist's Sanctum
cards.role: Repeatable planeswalker fuel from a land
cards.why: A land slot can supply blue mana early and repeated empower activations later.
cards.better: An existing Jace helps it enter untapped, and spare mana turns into continued loyalty.
cards.watch: Without beholding a Jace it enters tapped; activating it uses this land as well as three other mana.
